Finally, we’ll delve into the integration of plant maintenance with SAP EWM,
SAP’s influential warehouse management system (WMS). This integration plays a
pivotal role in facilitating the seamless and efficient handling of goods issue and
goods receipt processes within the plant maintenance procedure. By the end of
this chapter, you’ll have a comprehensive understanding of plant maintenance
and its integration with SAP EWM for both outbound goods issues and inbound
return processes.
9.1 Overview of Plant Maintenance
Plant maintenance encompasses a range of activities to help an organization
manage its technical systems effectively. These activities include inspection,
preventive maintenance, and repair, among other measures.
Inspection involves conducting a thorough assessment of the current condition
of a technical system. This task involves checking the equipment and
components of the system to identify any potential issues or areas of concern.
The data collected from inspections can be used to create maintenance plans to
address the specific needs of the system.
Preventive maintenance aims to keep technical systems in an ideal condition by
regularly carrying out routine maintenance activities. This area includes tasks
like cleaning, lubricating, adjusting, and replacing components before they fail.
By implementing preventive maintenance, your organization can reduce the risk
of breakdowns and extend equipment lifespans.
Repair involves fixing any issues that arise within the technical system to restore
it to its ideal condition. This activity can involve replacing defective components,
repairing broken equipment, or adjusting components that are not working
properly. Repair work is usually carried out in response to an identified problem
or issue.
Other measures taken using the plant maintenance capabilities can include
planning and scheduling maintenance tasks, monitoring equipment
performance, and managing spare parts inventory. These activities support the
overall goal of keeping technical systems functioning efficiently and effectively.

488
In general, the plant maintenance business process involves the following end-
to-end functions:
Request initiation
A maintenance request is generated indicating the need for maintenance or
repair work to be performed at an external location. This request can come
from various sources such as equipment operators, technicians, or
automated monitoring systems.
Work order creation
Based on the maintenance request, a work order is created, specifying the
details of the task, including the equipment or system to be repaired, the
location, the required resources, and any relevant documentation or
procedures.
Resource allocation
The necessary resources for the maintenance task are identified and
allocated. These resources might include skilled technicians, specialized tools
or equipment, spare parts, and transportation arrangements to reach the
external location.
Planning and scheduling
The maintenance task is planned and scheduled, considering factors such as
technician availability, priority of the task, and the logistics of reaching the
external site. The schedule should optimize efficiency and minimize
downtime.
Dispatching and logistics
Once the schedule is finalized, the work order is dispatched to the assigned
technicians or maintenance crew. Logistics arrangements, such as arranging
transportation or providing detailed directions to the external site, are made
to ensure timely arrival.
Execution
Technicians travel to the external site and carry out the maintenance or repair
work according to the specifications outlined in the work order. They may
perform inspections, diagnostics, troubleshooting, repairs, replacements, or
any other necessary tasks to restore the equipment or system to proper
working condition.
Documentation and reporting
Throughout the process, technicians document their activities, findings, and
© 

489
any changes made during the maintenance task. This information is recorded
for future reference, analysis, and compliance purposes. After completing the
task, technicians prepare reports summarizing their work and any additional
recommendations.
Follow-up actions
Depending on the findings during the maintenance task, further actions may
be required. These actions can include ordering additional parts, scheduling
follow-up visits, or updating preventive maintenance plans to prevent similar
issues in the future.
Closure and feedback
Once the maintenance task is completed, the work order is closed, and
relevant stakeholders are notified. Feedback from technicians, customers, or
site representatives may be collected to assess the quality of the maintenance
work and identify areas for improvement.
Overall, plant maintenance activities are crucial for ensuring that technical
systems remain operational and reliable. By conducting inspections,
implementing preventive maintenance, carrying out repairs, and taking other
necessary measures, your organization can keep its equipment functioning
optimally and minimize downtimes.
Plant maintenance seamlessly integrates with other components of the SAP ERP
system, including materials management, quality management, production
planning, sales and distribution, finance, controlling, and human resources.
By integrating with other modules, such as materials management, production,
sales and distribution, personnel management, and controlling, plant
maintenance ensures that data is always up-to-date. This integration also
triggers necessary processes in plant maintenance and customer service in other
areas of the SAP ERP system. For example, when you need to purchase a non-
stock material, a purchase requisition is automatically generated in the
materials management/purchasing area. The integration of plant maintenance
with other SAP ERP modules ensures that the data in each module remains up-
to-date and can trigger processes in other functions as necessary.
The cornerstone of plant maintenance is its master data, which is stored in and
managed through centralized master data tables. Within plant maintenance,
various types of master data exist, including equipment, functional locations,
specifications for objects, characteristics, task lists, codes containing
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

490
maintenance history data, material bills of materials (BOMs), measuring points,
and captured data about equipment use, such as wear and tear or consumption.
This master data serves as the foundation for creating transactional data in SAP
ERP. For instance, plant maintenance can use master data to create a
maintenance record, material management can create a purchase order,
production planning can create a production order, and sales and distribution
can create a sales order.
The integration of SAP EWM with plant maintenance through SAP Enterprise
Asset Management (SAP EAM) enables you to easily use and adapt the system,
resulting in a fast time-to-value and a low total cost of ownership (TCO). SAP EWM
offers many advantages for streamlining warehouse operations, increasing
productivity, and improving accuracy. Meanwhile, plant maintenance (in SAP
EAM) automates the process of handling facility repair and maintenance
requests for assets. Plant maintenance order-driven warehouse operations are
crucial for ensuring the timely availability of spare parts and for reducing repair
time.
The primary goal of integrating plant maintenance with SAP EWM is to enhance
efficiency, integration, and visibility throughout warehouse execution as well as
reap the following benefits:
Successful deployment of an improved integration package across multiple
customer locations.
Flexibility to incorporate customer-specific requirements from plant
maintenance orders for integration and warehouse operations.
Two integration approach options—the delivery-based option and the
production material request (PMR)-based option—can be pursued, depending
on the type of industry (i.e., mining, oil & gas, or manufacturing) and the
complexity of the customer process.
Leveraging SAP EWM’s standard warehouse process capability and
functionalities for all core processes, including handheld radio frequency (RF)
devices.
Optimizing warehouse operations by utilizing consolidation and cross-
docking based on plant maintenance orders.
Process and industry expertise in plant maintenance orders and warehouse
management.

Let’s briefly discuss these two integration approaches:
Delivery-based integration
This option is primarily used for the maintenance of heavy engineering assets,
such as in the mining and oil & gas industries. As shown in Figure 9.2,
delivery-based integration for plant maintenance mainly covers following
high-level processes:
Creation and release of plant maintenance orders for pick parts in SAP
S/4HANA
Creation of an outbound delivery and its replication in SAP EWM
Creation of waves for pick parts, based on the outbound delivery order in
SAP EWM
Picking, staging, and loading plant maintenance parts from warehouses in
SAP EWM
Performing goods issues in SAP EWM
Updating material document and reservation data for the plant
maintenance order in SAP S/4HANA
Figure 9.2 Delivery-Based Integration

PMR-based integration
This option is primarily used for the maintenance of production assets in
manufacturing plants, such as automotive and consumer goods.
The PMR-based integration option is not available as an out-of-the-box SAP
EWM solution. To use this functionality, an add-on from SAP Consulting is
available for the integration with PMR. As shown in Figure 9.3, a plant
maintenance order using PMR has several features including the following:
A new object, called the production material request, offers greater
flexibility in staging processes within SAP EWM.
The new EWM staging option has been added to the control cycle in
addition to the existing pick parts and release order part options.
The system supports single-order staging, cross-order staging, and manual
staging.
Status and quantity updates for manufacturing orders are supported.
The system allows for user-driven staging via desktop transactions or
staging in the background.

9.2 Using Plant Maintenance Orders
In this section, we’ll show you how to use plant maintenance for goods issues
and goods receipts. We’ll begin with the outbound process and then cover the
inbound process. For both scenarios, we’ll walk through the business process,
configuration, and master data setup needed and then provide a process
demonstration.
9.2.1 Outbound Process
In this section, we’ll thoroughly explore the outbound goods issue process using
plant maintenance orders with the delivery-based integration deployment
option. This section is divided into four parts: business process, configuration
required for the process, master data, and step-by-step process flow.
Business Process
An outbound process in plant maintenance typically refers to activities involved
in the maintenance and repair of equipment, machinery, or infrastructure
outside of the plant or facility where they are located. This process involves
coordinating and managing the necessary resources, personnel, and materials
to execute maintenance tasks at external sites.
The overall business process for a goods issue of a material to a maintenance
order is shown in Figure 9.4. The key steps involved in an outbound process with
plant maintenance include the following:
1. The outbound process typically starts in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA when a
maintenance order is created. The outbound delivery is created with
reference to the maintenance order. The outbound delivery is created in
SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA but is automatically is replicated to SAP EWM for
further processing.
2. In SAP EWM, a wave is created for the outbound delivery order. Upon wave
release, a warehouse task to pick the material is automatically created. The
pick warehouse task is based on the picking strategy for the plant
maintenance material.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@cbccom.com

494
Figure 9.4 Outbound Process Using Plant Maintenance Orders
3. The plant maintenance material is further picked, packed, and loaded as
per the warehouse process. Once the process is completed, the warehouse
team performs goods the issue for the outbound delivery order, and the
outbound process is completed.
4. The plant maintenance team consumes the material, and the cost of the
material is booked against the maintenance order.
By following these steps, the outbound process in plant maintenance ensures
effective management of maintenance tasks at external sites, enabling the
timely resolution of equipment or system issues to maintain operational
efficiency and reliability.
Configuration
In this section, we’ll cover the key customization options required for this
process, assuming that the main SAP EWM customization settings have already
been configured in the system:
1. Activate the business configuration (BC) set for the outbound process in
SAP EWM
In this configuration setting, the BC set will be activated. Follow the IMG
menu path Tools • Customizing • Business Configuration Sets • Activation
of BC Sets. Maintain the BC Set field and click Activate, as shown in
Figure 9.5. Then, click Save.

9.2.2 Inbound Process
In this section, we’ll thoroughly explore the inbound return goods receipt
process by utilizing SAP S/4HANA, SAP EWM. This section is divided into four
© 

507
parts: inbound goods receipt business process, configuration needed for the
process, master data, and step-by-step process flow.
Business Process
The goods receipt process with plant maintenance involves receiving and
recording goods or materials delivered to a plant or facility, as well as managing
any associated maintenance activities. The maintenance return order process
with SAP EWM typically involves several steps to ensure the smooth return of
goods for maintenance or repair purposes.
As shown in Figure 9.29, this process involves the following steps:
1. The process begins with the creation of a maintenance return order in SAP
EWM. This order is generated to initiate the return process and includes
relevant details such as the material, quantity, and reason for return as well
as any specific instructions.
2. A maintenance order is changed in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA to initiate the
process of returning goods to the store. During the process of goods receipt,
an inbound delivery will be created, which is then replicated to SAP EWM in
the background.
3. When the material is physically received in the warehouse, the warehouse
team generates a warehouse task and physically places the material in the
storage area in the SAP EWM system. A putaway strategy is defined for plant
maintenance materials, guiding warehouse operators to physically store the
material in the designated area and confirm the warehouse task
accordingly.
4. Upon arrival at the warehouse, the returned materials are received into the
SAP EWM system. The goods receipt process involves capturing information
such as the quantity received, inspection details (if applicable), and any
discrepancies identified during the inspection
5. After the material is stored in the designated area, the warehouse team
performs a goods receipt in SAP EWM, which generates inventory in both the
SAP EWM and SAP S/4HANA systems
6. The plant maintenance team can now further book labor hours, and the
maintenance order is technically complete.

SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals offers invaluable
assistance to pharmaceutical companies in fulfilling their specific legal
obligations regarding the serialization, tracking, and tracing of products
as well as in diligently reporting compliance with pharmaceutical product
regulations from the relevant regulatory bodies. Moreover, this solution
facilitates seamless data exchanges with packaging lines and enhances
collaboration with supply chain partners, such as warehouse operations,
third-party logistics (3PL), and contract manufacturing organizations
(CMOs). SAP Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals seamlessly
integrates with diverse business processes, enterprise resource planning
(ERP) systems, transactions, warehouse management, and supply chain
management, thereby streamlining operations comprehensively. By
placing paramount emphasis on patient safety, SAP Advanced Track and
Trace for Pharmaceuticals helps protect company reputations.
Furthermore, the meticulous management of serial numbers presents a
formidable challenge for counterfeiters attempting to replicate legitimate
codes, thereby serving as a deterrent against fraud. The primary aim of
this chapter is to provide comprehensive information regarding SAP
Advanced Track and Trace for Pharmaceuticals.
SAP Extended Warehouse Management (SAP EWM) and SAP Advanced Track and
Trace for Pharmaceuticals can be seamlessly integrated to deliver complete end-
to-end visibility and control over the storage and movement of pharmaceutical
products within warehouses and distribution centers.
In typical business scenarios, whenever a serialized item is moved in or out of a
warehouse, it is imperative to update both the stock management and the
serialization repository accordingly. However, updating these two separate
systems separately poses a significant risk of data inconsistency. The Warehouse
integration feature addresses this issue by enabling the integration of
warehouse stock with the serialization repository, ensuring data consistency and
minimizing the risk of errors. This integration feature facilitates the
